hints.title: Connected Component Representation
hints.text: A stone can be removed if another stone shares its row or column. Model stones sharing rows or columns as belonging to the same connected component.

hints.title: Component Size and Removals
hints.text: In any connected component of size k, we can always remove k minus 1 stones in sequence, leaving exactly 1 stone behind.

hints.title: Disjoint Set Coordinate Union
hints.text: Treat row r and column c as nodes in a graph. For each stone at (r, c), connect r with ~c (bitwise inversion of c). The maximum stones removed equals total stones minus the number of connected components.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Exploring all removal permutations yields factorial complexity O(N!), whereas connected components solve it directly.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Connecting rows and column indices in disjoint sets requires linear memory and near-constant time operations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should show that connected graph components always collapse to a single representative node.
complexity.notes: Using ~c differentiates column indices from row indices without collisions.
